title: Choose the visual world for SAKSAVI
question: Your coconut story (grow → fall → truck → world) is fixed in every option. This picks the world that frames it. The roll dealt The Bill of Lading: keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Bill of Lading
options.lineage: Ocean bills of lading, shipping instructions and violet office rubber stamps
options.thesis: The site is the shipment's own paperwork: every scroll fills a field, and the enquiry is the consignment form.
materials: illustrated grove scenes behind the form
options.viewport: Full-bleed illustrated palm grove in deep green; numbered document boxes frame it; a working 'shipping instruction' quote form sits bottom-right.
options.risk: If the document grammar is applied timidly it reads as a dull form; it has to be confident, oversized and stamped.

raised.raise: One unbroken route line runs the full page with a single marker for 'now'.
Hierarchy by scale alone: tiny form labels, one huge filled value per box.
Each stage arrives bright along its arrow while the previous stage stays ghosted.
One transformation per phone viewport, text readable throughout.
Violet stamp ink is reserved for confirmed states only, never decoration.
The scene's centre stays empty for the coconut; readouts live in the corners.

options.label: Grove-to-Sea Diorama
options.thesis: One deep layered landscape you travel through, from grove to highway to port to open sea.
materials: cut-paper layers with soft drop shadows
options.viewport: A golden-hour grove in five paper layers, a big headline in the sky and the quote action pinned top-right.
options.risk: Familiar: this is where most illustrated-parallax sites in this category land.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.thesis: The supply chain as numbered assembly steps.
options.viewport: Step 1 of the chain as an exploded diagram.
options.case: Clear process, but importers don't see themselves in a toy booklet.
options.risk: Reads as a toy, not a supplier.
options.kept: Prior stage ghosted, new stage arrives bright along its arrow.

options.label: Step Row
options.thesis: Shipments as a programmable step sequence.
options.viewport: A sixteen-step row of the year's harvests.
options.case: No buyer identification and the coconut story gets lost.
options.risk: Pure novelty for a B2B exporter.
options.kept: One unbroken timeline with a single 'now' marker.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: The brand told through one morphing letter.
options.case: Says nothing about coconuts or supply.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.viewport: Letters raining into the word COCONUT.
options.case: Too abstract for a buyer checking reliability.

options.label: Painted Hoarding
options.thesis: The harvest as a held cinematic moment.
options.viewport: A climber frozen mid-leap at the palm crown.
options.case: Wrong cultural home for a South Indian exporter.
options.kept: One ink reserved for one meaning.

options.label: Viewfinder HUD
options.thesis: Watching the harvest through a camera.
options.viewport: Focus brackets around a falling coconut.
options.case: Gimmicky; buyers want the product, not the camera.
options.kept: Centre kept empty for the subject.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean agro-exporter site, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and quote button on the left, coconut cluster on the right, product cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other exporter by design.
